mainTopic: Hidden flawed lineage, ה׳'s secret names, and presumed lineage status in בבל, ארץ ישראל and other lands
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching: when ה׳ clears up the lineage of the tribes, He starts with שבט לוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי adds that money helps ממזרים blend into regular families. רבי יצחק calls it a kindness that a family which has already blended in stays blended in. The גמרא then backs שמואל's ranking that lineage is most reliable in בבל, then ארץ ישראל, then other lands, with stories about רבי and רבי פנחס. רבי יוחנן, אביי and a ברייתא show that the חכמים chose not to expose families with hidden flaws, sharing such names only privately and rarely. This leads to a side discussion of ה׳'s secret names, the four-letter, twelve-letter and forty-two-letter names, and how carefully they were guarded. Finally, שמואל gives the presumed lineage status of families in בבל, other lands and ארץ ישראל. The גמרא challenges the ארץ ישראל rule as contradicting itself, and רב הונא בר תחליפא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The tribe of Levi is purified first
steps.stepSummary: When הקדוש ברוך הוא clears up the lineage of the tribes, He starts with שבט לוי, based on a פסוק in מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When He purifies the tribes, He will purify the tribe of Levi first, as it says: 'And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and refine them like gold and silver, and they shall be for ה׳ bringers of offerings in righteousness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started on the previous daf: in the future, ה׳ will sort out family lineage, and He will begin with שבט לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that the פסוק names בני לוי as the first ones to be 'purified'. Lineage matters most for לויים and כהנים, because they serve in the מקדש. The rest of this פסוק becomes the basis for the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: purifies; here it means clarifying a family's true lineage
a refiner, someone who removes impurities from metal
and he will refine or purge

phrases.english: purifies the tribes,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the end of the last daf: 'When הקדוש ברוך הוא purifies the tribes...'

phrases.english: He will purify the tribe of Levi first,
as it is stated: "And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver,
and he shall purify the sons of Levi,
and refine them like gold and like silver,
and they shall be for ה׳ bringers of offerings in righteousness."

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי מְטַהֵר תְּחִילָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a statement begun on the previous daf about ה׳ purifying the tribes' lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future clarification of lineage, שבט לוי is purified first.

steps.title: Money helps ממזרים blend in
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the same פסוק as teaching that money makes ממזרים blend into regular families.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: Money purifies ממזרים, as it says: 'And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a new reading of the same פסוק: rich ממזרים end up blending into regular Jewish families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Families marry wealthy ממזרים for their money, so over time their flawed lineage is hidden. He reads 'מטהר כסף' as 'silver purifies', so the money itself causes the 'purifying'. In the future ה׳ will not single these families out.

keyTerms.meaning: people born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into regular Jewish families

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean money makes a ממזר permitted by הלכה. It means wealthy ממזר families blend in, and their status stays hidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
Money purifies mamzerim,
phrases.notes: Families marry rich ממזרים for their money, so these families blend in with everyone else.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver."
phrases.notes: He reads 'purifier of silver' as 'silver purifies'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כֶּסֶף מְטַהֵר מַמְזֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 1 to teach a new idea about ממזרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money causes wealthy ממזרים to blend into families of proper lineage.

steps.title: What does 'offerings in righteousness' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the end of the פסוק, 'bringers of offerings in righteousness', fits this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'bringers of offerings in righteousness' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step: what is the 'righteousness' at the end of the פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is about families with flawed lineage blending in, the word 'צדקה' needs an explanation. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: What is meant by "bringers of offerings in righteousness"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״מַגִּישֵׁי מִנְחָה בִּצְדָקָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the final words of the פסוק quoted in steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'בצדקה' at the end of the פסוק.

steps.title: A blended family stays blended
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that ה׳ did a kindness: a family that already blended in is not exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: ה׳ did an act of righteousness with Israel, that a family that has blended in stays blended in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: the 'righteousness' is that a family with flawed lineage that has already blended in will not be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of exposing every hidden family problem, ה׳ leaves families that are fully mixed in alone. This protects the many people who married into them without knowing. It fits with step 2: families that blended in are not singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: He did an act of kindness
became mixed in or blended in

steps.whatToRemember: A family with flawed lineage that has already fully blended into Israel stays blended in. This is called a צדקה (kindness) that ה׳ does for Israel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:

phrases.aramaic: צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, did an act of righteousness with Israel,
that a family that has blended in, stays blended in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'righteousness' is that a family that has blended in is left alone and not exposed.

steps.title: Ranking lineage: בבל, then ארץ ישראל, then other lands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's rule: other lands are 'mixed' compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is 'mixed' compared to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: All lands are dough compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is dough compared to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word 'גופא', the גמרא goes back to a statement it mentioned earlier and now looks at it directly. שמואל ranks where Jewish lineage is most reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עיסה' (dough) means mixed and doubtful lineage. בבל has the most reliable lineage, ארץ ישראל is next, and all other lands are last. So a person from a higher place marrying someone from a lower place would need to check that family's lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': going back to a statement quoted earlier

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
All lands are dough compared to Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: 'Dough' means mixed up, like flour and water you can't separate, so the lineage there is doubtful.

phrases.english: and Eretz Yisrael is dough compared to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the פסוק and goes back to a statement of שמואל that was quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lineage in בבל is the most reliable, then ארץ ישראל, then all other lands.

steps.title: An attempt to rank ארץ ישראל above בבל
steps.stepSummary: In רבי's time, some wanted to call בבל 'mixed' compared to ארץ ישראל. רבי objected and sent them to רבי חנינא בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי, they wanted to make בבל dough compared to ארץ ישראל. He said to them: Are you putting thorns between my eyes? If you want, רבי חנינא בר חמא will deal with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an attempt to reverse שמואל's ranking. רבי refuses and sends them to רבי חנינא בר חמא, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of ארץ ישראל wanted their own lineage ranked higher than בבל's. רבי's family came from הלל, who was from בבל, so he felt this would be an insult to him ('thorns between my eyes'). Instead of ruling himself, he lets רבי חנינא בר חמא answer them.

keyTerms.meaning: in the days of רבי יהודה הנשיא
thorns; here, something painful or insulting
will deal with you; will take up the matter with you

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi, they sought
to make Babylonia dough compared to Eretz Yisrael.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: קוֹצִים אַתֶּם מְשִׂימִים לִי בֵּין עֵינַי?
phrases.english: He said to them: Are you putting thorns between my eyes?
phrases.notes: רבי's family came from הלל, who was from בבל, so this felt like an insult to him.

phrases.aramaic: רְצוֹנְכֶם, יִטָּפֵל עִמָּכֶם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא.
phrases.english: If you wish, Rabbi Chanina bar Chama will deal with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי בִּקְּשׁוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּבֶל עִיסָּה לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about an attempt to reverse the ranking stated in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי refused to accept a reversed ranking and passed the matter to רבי חנינא בר חמא.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בר חמא confirms the ranking from tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר חמא cites a tradition from רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, in his father's name, that matches שמואל's ranking exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר חמא took the matter up with them and said: This is what I received from רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, who said in his father's name: All lands are dough compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is dough compared to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר חמא ends the attempt by quoting a received tradition. It says exactly what שמואל said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is strong because it comes from רבי יוסי, a sage of ארץ ישראל. Even a sage from ארץ ישראל admitted that בבל's lineage is more reliable. So the ranking of step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: took up the matter; engaged with them
I have received this as a tradition
in the name of his father

steps.whatToRemember: The ranking stands: בבל has the most reliable lineage, then ארץ ישראל, then all other lands. This is backed both by שמואל and by a tradition from רבי יוסי, a sage of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: נִטְפַּל עִמָּהֶם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Chama took the matter up with them,
and said to them: This is what I have received
from Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
who said in the name of his father:
All lands are dough compared to Eretz Yisrael,
and Eretz Yisrael is dough compared to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְפַּל עִמָּהֶם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא, אָמַר לָהֶם: כָּךְ מְקוּבְּלַנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out what רבי suggested in step 6 and rejects the attempt to reverse the ranking.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ranking that ארץ ישראל is 'dough' compared to בבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition from רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי in the name of his father, רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי פנחס plans a quick escape
steps.stepSummary: People wanted to call בבל 'mixed' compared to ארץ ישראל. רבי פנחס told his servants to carry him away right after he said two things. His first statement was a surprising הלכה about birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי פנחס, people wanted to call בבל 'mixed dough' compared to ארץ ישראל. He told his servants: 'When I say two things in the בית המדרש, pick me up on a stretcher and run.' When he came in, he said: 'The Torah does not require שחיטה for a bird.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story, much like the story about רבי in step 6. This part sets up the scene: רבי פנחס plans ahead because he knows his main statement will make people angry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פנחס expects that defending בבל's lineage will upset powerful people in ארץ ישראל, so he arranges a getaway. His first statement, about שחיטה for birds, is a surprising הלכה. It keeps the scholars busy so he can deliver his second, more dangerous statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'dough.' It means a population whose family lines are mixed and doubtful.
Here, a stretcher or couch used to carry a person.

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Pinchas
they sought to make Babylonia
'mixed dough' compared to Eretz Yisrael.
phrases.notes: This is the same idea as step 6: they wanted to rank בבל's lineage below ארץ ישראל's.

phrases.english: He said to his servants:
When I say two things
in the study hall,
pick me up on a stretcher and run.
When he entered, he said to them:
There is no requirement of slaughter for a bird from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בִּקְּשׁוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּבֶל עִיסָּה לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that parallels step 6, again about the attempt to lower בבל's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי פנחס sets up a getaway before making a statement he knows will be dangerous.

steps.title: רבי פנחס defends בבל and escapes
steps.stepSummary: While the scholars were busy with the bird ruling, רבי פנחס stated שמואל's ranking and was carried away. The scholars began checking family lines but stopped when it became dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they sat analyzing that ruling, he said: 'All lands are mixed compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is mixed compared to בבל.' His servants carried him off and ran. People chased him but did not catch him. They sat and checked family lines until they reached danger, and then they stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס makes his second statement, the same ranking שמואל gave in step 5, and escapes. The people then try to check family lineage but give up because it is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story confirms שמואל's ranking: בבל's lineage is the purest. The checking stopped at 'danger.' This means the questionable families were powerful, and exposing them would put people at risk. That sets up רבי יוחנן's statement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They checked and investigated family lines.

phrases.english: While they were sitting and analyzing it,
he said to them:
All lands are mixed compared to Eretz Yisrael,
and Eretz Yisrael is mixed compared to Babylonia.
They picked him up on the stretcher and ran.
People ran after him but did not catch him.
They sat and checked
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say what they checked, but it means the family lines in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: until they reached danger, and they stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּיָתְבִי וְקָמְעַיְּינִי בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes the story of רבי פנחס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי פנחס repeats שמואל's ranking. Investigating lineage was stopped because it was dangerous.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן chooses not to expose a family
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן swears that he could reveal a flawed family, but he won't, because the great people of the generation have blended into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'By the Sanctuary! It is in our power to reveal it. But what can I do? The great people of the generation have blended into it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says he knows which family has a flawed lineage, but he will stay quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not a lack of information. רבי יוחנן knows the truth. He holds back because important people have already married into that family, so exposing it would hurt them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By the Sanctuary!' This is a form of oath.
In our hands, meaning we are able to do it.
The great people of the generation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: By the Sanctuary!
It is in our power,
phrases.notes: He means it is in our power to reveal which family has the flawed lineage.

phrases.english: but what can I do,
since the great people of the generation have blended into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֵיכְלָא, בְּיָדֵינוּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like the end of the story in step 9, a great sage chooses not to expose lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who knows of a hidden flawed lineage should not reveal it once it has blended in.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's silence follows רבי יצחק's rule: a family that blended in stays blended in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יצחק, who said: 'A family that has blended in has blended in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us the source behind רבי יוחנן's choice. It is the rule of רבי יצחק we saw in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי יוחנן's personal decision into a clear rule. Once a family's flaw has disappeared into the community, we leave it alone and do not dig it up.

keyTerms.meaning: A family that has blended in.

steps.whatToRemember: מִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁנִּטְמְעָה – נִטְמְעָה: once a flawed family has quietly blended in, we do not expose it.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yitzchak,
as Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A family that has blended in has blended in.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which earlier opinion רבי יוחנן's statement is based on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יצחק: a family that blended in stays blended in.

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה about בן ציון and אליהו
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה about two families that בן ציון treated wrongly by force. אליהו will come in the future to fix such cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'We also learned this in a משנה: The family of בית הצריפה was across the ירדן, and בן ציון pushed it away by force. There was another family that בן ציון brought close by force. For families like these, אליהו comes to declare impure and pure, to push away and bring close.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה to support רבי יצחק's rule. This step quotes the משנה, and the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says אליהו will correct the status of families like these. That might sound like אליהו will expose every flawed family. אביי is about to show that the words 'like these' limit it.

keyTerms.meaning: We too learned this in a משנה. It introduces support.
Pushed it away, declaring it unfit.
Brought it close, declaring it fit.
אליהו will come in the future to clarify things.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too learned this in a Mishnah:
The family of Beit HaTzerifa
was across the Jordan,
and Ben Tziyon pushed it away by force.
There was another one,
and Ben Tziyon brought it close by force.
For ones like these, Elijah comes
to declare impure and to declare pure, to push away and to bring close.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבי יצחק's rule from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that a family that blended in stays blended in.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עדיות about בן ציון and what אליהו will do.

steps.title: Only known cases will be fixed
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'like these' means families whose situation is known. A family that quietly blended in stays blended in, even when אליהו comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Like these' means families that are known. But a family that has blended in has blended in.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reads the words of the משנה closely to finish his proof. This completes his support for רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ציון's families were well known, so their wrong status was public, and אליהו will fix it. A family whose flaw is unknown is not included, so even אליהו will not expose it. This confirms רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: אליהו will fix only well-known lineage cases. A flaw that has quietly blended in stays hidden forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how far the הלכה protects families. If even אליהו will not expose a hidden flaw, then we certainly should not.

phrases.english: 'Like these' means ones that are known,
but a family that has blended in has blended in.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן אֵלּוּ דְּיָדְעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'like these' in the משנה so the proof works.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only known lineage cases will be corrected. A family that blended in stays blended in, supporting רבי יצחק and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Another flawed family the Sages kept secret
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that there was one more flawed family. The חכמים did not reveal it publicly, but they passed its name to their children and students once, or twice, every seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: There was another family, and the Sages did not want to reveal it. But the Sages pass it on to their children and students once every seven years, and some say twice every seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about one more family with a flawed lineage that the חכמים kept quiet about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier steps, where flawed families that blended in were left alone. The חכמים still shared the name privately, so their own children and students would not marry into that family. There are two opinions on how often they shared it.
steps.confusionAlert: Here בשבוע does not mean 'in a week.' It means a seven-year cycle, like the שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: It was taught: There was another one,
phrases.notes: He means another family with a flawed lineage, like the ones discussed just before.

phrases.english: and the Sages did not want to reveal it.
But the Sages pass it on
to their children and to their students
once every seven years,
and some say twice every seven years.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּאנָא: עוֹד אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of a flawed family kept secret, continuing the theme of steps 10-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flawed family's name is kept private and passed only to children and students, once or twice every seven years.

steps.title: Once every seven years makes more sense, proven from a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the 'once' opinion is more reasonable. He proves it from a ברייתא: a person who vowed to be a נזיר unless he reveals families should keep his נזירות and not reveal them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense like the one who says once every seven years. As it is taught: 'I am a נזיר if I do not reveal families' — he should be a נזיר and not reveal families.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק picks between the two opinions and brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows how serious it is to reveal flawed families. A person should even accept a whole נזירות rather than expose them. So the less often the name is shared, the better, which supports 'once.'

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, it is reasonable
as it is taught in a ברייתא
I am hereby a נזיר (a vow)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It makes sense like the one who says
once every seven years.
As it is taught:
'I am hereby a nazir if I do not reveal families' —
he should be a nazir, and not reveal families.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשָׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions given in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the family's name is shared only once every seven years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one who vows נזירות unless he reveals families should be a נזיר and not reveal them.

steps.title: The four-letter name is also taught rarely
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the חכמים pass on the four-letter name of ה׳ to their students once, or twice, every seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The four-letter name — the חכמים pass it on to their students once every seven years, and some say twice every seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic: another secret that the חכמים passed on just as rarely, the four-letter name of ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same 'once or twice every seven years' pattern is used here. The topic is now how to correctly say the holy name, not family lines. Again there are two opinions about how often.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The four-letter name —
phrases.notes: He means how to say this name correctly.

phrases.english: the Sages pass it on to their students
once every seven years,
and some say twice every seven years.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׁם בֶּן אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת חֲכָמִים מוֹסְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same secrecy pattern from step 14 for a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four-letter name is taught to students only once or twice every seven years.

steps.title: Once makes more sense, because the name must be hidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק again prefers 'once.' He brings a פסוק: 'זה שמי לעולם' is written in a way that can be read לעלם, 'to hide.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense like the one who says once every seven years, as it is written: 'This is My name forever' — it is written 'to hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: Just like in step 15, רב נחמן בר יצחק supports 'once,' this time with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם (forever) is written without a ו, so it can also be read לעלם (to hide). This shows the name is meant to stay hidden, so the less often it is taught, the better.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשָׁבוּעַ,
phrases.english: It makes sense like the one who says once every seven years,
as it is written: 'This is My name forever,'
it is written 'to hide.'
phrases.notes: The word is spelled without a ו, so the same letters can be read as 'to hide.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשָׁבוּעַ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the four-letter name is taught only once every seven years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 3:15 — לעולם is written so it can be read לעלם, 'to hide.'

steps.title: An elder stops רבא from teaching the name in public
steps.stepSummary: רבא planned to explain the name in a public lecture. An elder reminded him that the פסוק says the name should be hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא planned to teach it in a public lecture. A certain elder said to him: It is written 'to hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows the rule from step 17 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא wanted to teach the name to a large crowd. The elder used the same reading, לעלם, to warn him. The story shows the name must not be taught publicly.

keyTerms.meaning: to teach it, to explain it

phrases.english: Rava planned to teach it in a public lecture.
A certain elder said to him:
It is written 'to hide.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא סָבַר לְמִידְרְשֵׁיהּ בְּפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that uses the proof from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The holy name may not be taught in a public lecture, because it must be kept hidden.

steps.title: רבי אבינא: Is it 'My name' or 'My remembrance'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא points out that the same פסוק calls it both 'My name' and 'My remembrance,' which seem to clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא pointed out a contradiction: It is written 'This is My name,' and it is written 'This is My remembrance.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא raises a contradiction between two parts of the same פסוק. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My name' sounds like the written name is the real name. 'My remembrance' sounds like it is only a way to remember the name. Which one is it?

keyTerms.meaning: My remembrance, how I am mentioned

phrases.english: Rabbi Avina pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: 'This is My name,'
and it is written: 'This is My remembrance.'
phrases.notes: Both phrases come from the same פסוק, שמות 3:15.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבִינָא רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks again at the same פסוק used in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two phrases in שמות 3:15: 'זה שמי' and 'זה זכרי.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase calls it the actual name; the other calls it only a way of remembering. They seem to clash.

steps.title: Written one way, said another way
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ה׳ says His name is not said the way it is written. It is written יוד הי and said אלף דלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Not as I am written am I read. I am written with יוד הי, and read with אלף דלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבינא's contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My name' is how it is written (the four-letter name). 'My remembrance' is how it is said out loud (אדני). Both are true, just about different things.
steps.whatToRemember: The four-letter name is written one way but read aloud as אדני; this is why the name stays hidden.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Not as I am written am I read.
I am written with yod heh,
phrases.notes: Short for the full four-letter name, starting with יוד הי.

phrases.english: and read with alef dalet.
phrases.notes: Short for the name אדני, which starts with these letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two phrases: one is about writing, the other about speaking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases seem to describe the same name in clashing ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'My name' is the written form; 'My remembrance' is the spoken form, אדני.

steps.title: The twelve-letter name became restricted to modest כהנים
steps.stepSummary: At first, the twelve-letter name was taught to anyone. When disrespectful people grew many, it was taught only to modest כהנים, who said it quietly under their fellow כהנים' tune.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: At first, they would pass on the twelve-letter name to anyone. Once the unrestrained people grew many, they would pass it on only to the modest ones among the priests, and those modest priests would swallow it in the tune of their fellow priests.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells the history of how another holy name, the twelve-letter name, was handled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule changed because people misused the name. After that, only modest כהנים learned it. Even they hid it by saying it softly while the other כהנים were singing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: At first,
the twelve-letter name —
they would pass it on to any person.
Once the unrestrained people grew many,
they would pass it on to the modest ones among the priesthood,
and the modest ones among the priesthood
would swallow it
in the tune of their fellow priests.
phrases.notes: This happened during ברכת כהנים; the name was said softly while the others sang.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, שֵׁם בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the four-letter name to another secret name that was also kept hidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After people misused it, the twelve-letter name was taught only to modest כהנים, who said it quietly within the tune.

steps.title: רבי טרפון heard the כהן גדול hide the name
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says that once, when he went up to the platform after his uncle, he listened closely to the כהן גדול and heard him swallow the name in the other כהנים' tune.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי טרפון said: Once I went up after my mother's brother to the דוכן, and I bent my ear toward the כהן גדול, and I heard him swallow the name in the tune of his fellow כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי טרפון's eyewitness report, which supports the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the modest כהנים hid the name inside the tune. רבי טרפון actually heard this happen with the כהן גדול. Even someone listening closely only heard that the name was swallowed in the tune.

keyTerms.meaning: the platform where the כהנים stand for ברכת כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: Holy knowledge (flawed family lines and the secret names of ה׳) was guarded carefully: taught rarely, never publicly, and even said quietly.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Tarfon said:
Once I went up
after my mother's brother to the platform,
and I bent my ear toward the High Priest,
and I heard that he swallowed the name
in the tune of his fellow priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An eyewitness story that supports the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the כהנים swallowed the name within the tune of their fellow כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טרפון's personal report of hearing the כהן גדול on the דוכן.

steps.title: Who may be taught the forty-two-letter name
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quoting רב says the forty-two-letter name is given only to a modest, humble, mature, calm, sober and forgiving person. Whoever knows it and guards it in purity is loved above and below and inherits both worlds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The forty-two-letter name of ה׳ is passed on only to someone who is modest and humble, who has reached the middle of his life, who does not get angry, does not get drunk, and does not insist on his own way. Anyone who knows this name, is careful with it, and guards it in purity is loved in Heaven and treasured on earth. People are in awe of him, and he inherits two worlds, this world and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching about ה׳'s secret names. This time it is about an even longer name, the forty-two-letter name, and who may learn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the twelve-letter name was limited to modest כהנים. Here the forty-two-letter name has an even stricter list of required qualities. Each quality guards against the name being misused or let out, for example in anger or while drunk. The teaching ends with the great reward of someone who keeps the name pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The forty-two-letter name of ה׳, a hidden holy name
Insists on his own way and does not let things go

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the side discussion about ה׳'s secret names. The higher and holier the name, the stricter the requirements for the person who receives it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The forty-two-letter name
is not passed on
except to one who is modest and humble,
and stands at half his days,
and does not get angry, and does not get drunk,
and does not insist on his own way.
And anyone who knows it, and is careful with it,
and guards it in purity,
is loved above and treasured below,
and fear of him is placed on people,
and he inherits two worlds:
this world and the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֵׁם בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁתַּיִם אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series on secret names of ה׳. After the twelve-letter name (steps 21-22), it moves to the forty-two-letter name and closes the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forty-two-letter name may be taught only to a modest, humble, middle-aged person who does not get angry or drunk and who lets things go. One who guards it in purity is rewarded in both worlds.

steps.title: Presumed lineage in בבל, other lands, and ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoting an elder, says families in בבל are presumed כשר until shown otherwise, families in other lands are presumed פסול until shown otherwise, and in ארץ ישראל a family known as פסול is פסול and a family known as כשר is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of an elder: בבל is assumed to have proper lineage until you learn how a family there became flawed. Other lands are assumed to have flawed lineage until you learn how a family there became proper. In ארץ ישראל, a family known to be flawed is flawed, and a family known to be proper is proper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main topic, family lineage. It brings a rule about what status we assume for a family, depending on where it lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three regions with three different starting assumptions. In בבל the default is כשר, so you need proof of a problem. In other lands the default is פסול, so you need proof that the family is fine. For ארץ ישראל the rule only talks about families with a known status and does not clearly say what to do with an unknown family. That gap sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presumed status of; what we assume until shown otherwise
Proper, unflawed lineage; may marry into the Jewish people normally
An elder; here an unnamed older sage
Other lands, outside בבל and ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whose family background must be checked before marriage, and that is the core concern of this פרק.

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of an elder:
Babylonia stands with a presumption of being unflawed,
until it becomes known to you how it became flawed.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת – בְּחֶזְקַת פְּסוּל הֵן עוֹמְדוֹת,
phrases.english: Other lands stand with a presumption of being flawed,
until it becomes known to you how it became unflawed.
In Eretz Yisrael, one presumed flawed is flawed,
one presumed unflawed is unflawed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּסָבָא: בָּבֶל בְּחֶזְקַת כְּשֵׁרָה עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of ה׳'s names and returns to the main topic of family lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל is presumed כשר, other lands are presumed פסול, and in ארץ ישראל a family keeps whatever status it is known to have.

steps.title: The ארץ ישראל rule seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two halves of the ארץ ישראל rule imply opposite things about a family with no known status.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement itself is difficult! You said a family known to be flawed is flawed, so an unknown family must be proper. Then you teach that a family known to be proper is proper, so an unknown family must be flawed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last part of שמואל's rule, the part about ארץ ישראל. It shows that each half of that sentence points in an opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a family 'known as פסול' is פסול, then a family with no known status must be כשר. But if only a family 'known as כשר' is כשר, then a family with no known status must be פסול. The same sentence cannot hold both, so the rule needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
Known or presumed to have a certain status
Unspecified; a family with no known status
And then it goes on to teach

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about families whose status is known. Those are clear. It is only about a family with no known status, the 'סתמא', and what the rule implies for that family.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: one presumed flawed is flawed.
This implies an unspecified one is unflawed.
And then it teaches: one presumed unflawed is unflawed.
This implies an unspecified one is flawed!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפַאּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ארץ ישראל clause of the rule in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ארץ ישראל clause: 'מוחזק לפסול פסול, מוחזק לכשר כשר'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inferring from each half gives opposite results for an unknown family: the first half implies it is כשר, the second half implies it is פסול.

steps.title: רב הונא בר תחליפא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר תחליפא, quoting רב, opens his answer by saying there is no real contradiction. The explanation follows next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר תחליפא said in the name of רב: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the start of the answer to the contradiction. The גמרא is setting up the next move, and the actual explanation comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רב הונא בר תחליפא only declares that the two halves of the ארץ ישראל rule do not clash. The way he settles them, most likely by showing that each half talks about a different situation, is spelled out in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Taḥalifa said in the name of Rav:
It is not difficult,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the contradiction raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opening of the answer; the explanation follows after this line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the ארץ ישראל rule contradict each other about a family with no known status.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no real contradiction. How the two halves fit together is explained next.
